title: Boil-water, do-not-drink and do-not-use advisories
h1: What boil-water, do-not-drink and do-not-use advisories actually mean
dek: Three notices, three different dangers, and three different sets of rules. A room-by-room reading of the CDC's guidance, so you know what is still safe to do with tap water and what is not.
description: What the three types of drinking water advisory mean and what to do under each, from the CDC: drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, baby formula, dishes, bathing, pets.
recheck: If CDC revises the advisory page, or at the next quarterly source sweep. Always defer to the advisory your own utility issues.

source_use.cdc-water-advisories: The three advisory types; what each asks of a household; fridge water and ice; boil even if filtered; infant feeding; hygiene, dishes, laundry, pets and gardens; boiling does not fix chemicals.
source_use.cdc-find-clean-water: That officials may advise shutting off the main water valve, and that fuel- or chemical-contaminated water cannot be made safe.
source_use.cdc-water-safe: Boiling steps and the list of activities to avoid with unsafe water.
source_use.epa-emergency-disinfection: That local authorities may recommend bottled, boiled or disinfected water until regular service is restored.
